current.text: Walker Kessler is no longer with Utah, which leaves the starting center job open.
He re-signed with Utah for 2 years and 22 million.
Experts expect him to start at center for Utah, ahead of Ace Bailey and Kyle Filipowski. One expert says he is not 100% sure.
He ranked about 68th as a top-70 player when he started last season, after the Kessler injury.
If he starts, he should return at least top 80 numbers. One expert projects him at 27 minutes.

Experts say his market price in the 120s treats him like a backup. They call him a free pick and a strong late-round value who should beat his ADP comfortably. One expert would take him over Collins or Claxton.
Josh called him a risky pick when he took him in round 10 of a mock draft.
In a mock auction he sold for 9 USD. Josh, who is big on him, bid up to 8 USD.
His passing should matter more next to Jaren Jackson Jr. and Kyle Lowry, who do not pass much.
Utah is trying to win this season. Experts say tanking and shutdown fears are misplaced.
Utah has a crowded frontcourt and added Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba. Markkanen, Keyonte George, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Darryn Peterson take much of the usage.

durable.text: He rebounds well and is a good passer for a center.
He is not a high-usage player.
His FT% is far below the league and hurts a team's FT%.
He has a long history of knee, leg and other lower-body injuries.
Experts say his health record makes him hard to trust.

note: Yahoo ranks him 105 (4 USD value, 1.0 USD average cost) and ESPN ranks him 168, so he sits near the end of our 144-player pool. Experts see top 70 to 80 upside as Utah's starter, and one mock auction went to 9 USD. He is a cheap center for punt FT% builds, giving rebounds, assists and steals for a big, but his injury history makes a few dollars above Yahoo's value the sensible limit. Early in the season, check that he starts over Ace Bailey, plays close to the projected 27 minutes and stays healthy.
